Phase 8 is too large for one turn, so I split it. Phases 9 and 10 keep their numbers, so “OpenStreetMap after phase 9” still holds.

Sub-phase	Scope	Status
8a	GPS map panel in Compose	Written, not delivered
8b	Trail and measure map panels	Next
8c	Remaining dialogs, single activity with Navigation Compose, drop AppCompat themes	Planned
What 8a contains:

GPS panel rewritten: the fragment now only hosts a Compose screen. The toolbar, map tools, info sheet and speedometer are all Compose. The info sheet is a Material 3 bottom sheet in portrait and a side column in landscape.
Map lifecycle shared: a new MapLifecycle observer drives the map view, and the map search screen now uses it too. I removed the old early onResume() call from CustomMaps.onCreate.
Address lookups: they used to run a blocking geocoder call on every location fix. Now they use the non-blocking geocoder on Android 13+ and only run after the position moves at least 25 m, which should help battery.
Save location fix: saving now uses the shared database instance instead of opening a second one.
Navigate: if Google Maps isn’t installed, it now falls back to a generic geo: link.
Volume-key zoom: now handled through Compose key events.
New tests: GeoDistanceTest and SpeedometerDialTest.
README: the phase table is updated.
Deleted:
The old toolbar, tools, speedometer and popup classes.
10 GPS layouts.
The Speedometer styleable.
Three unused PaddingAware* views.
The ripple drawable.
The unused info_error string and info_text_item_line_spacing dimen, across all locales.
Reply “continue” and I’ll redo this, check it again, and deliver it as a tar.gz with one git rm command. As before, I can’t compile here, so CI is the real check.

On the OpenStreetMap fallback: no API key is needed. osmdroid with the standard OSM tiles works without one and caches viewed tiles on the device automatically. The catch is OSM’s tile usage policy. It requires a proper User-Agent (the app ID) and forbids bulk pre-downloading of areas, so “cache what you’ve looked at” is fine but “download this whole region for offline use” is not. Most vector-tile providers (MapTiler, Stadia) do need keys; OpenFreeMap is a keyless vector option if we want one later. My plan is to put the map behind a small interface during 8b, so swapping in osmdroid in phase 10 is a contained change.

Presented file
The archive is positional-phase8a.tar.gz. It contains the crash fix and the GPS panel from phase 8a. Extract it at the repo root; it holds only new and changed files.

Cause of the crash: the phase 7 Clock screen loaded the clock’s sweep trail through Compose’s image loader. That trail image is an XML shape, and Compose can only load vector images and bitmaps, so it throws as soon as the Clock panel is drawn. The app reopens on the last panel you used, so once you had opened Clock, every launch crashed. The time zone picker had the same problem with its “selected” dot (an XML layer-list), so it would also crash whenever a selected zone was on screen.

Fixes:

The sweep trail is now drawn directly with a sweep gradient.
The selected time zone dot is now a plain filled circle.
A new unit test, ComposeDrawablesTest, fails the build if any image drawn by Compose isn’t a vector or bitmap.
Other checks I made:

Every class name in a layout or the manifest points to a class that exists.
The phase 6 database changes are consistent with the stored schemas.
Rounding, list keys, sensor setup and the clock and sky calculations hold up.
Nothing else turned up that would crash at launch. I still can’t build or run the app here, so CI and your phone are the real test. If it still crashes, a stack trace from adb logcat would let me pin it down.

Phase 8a, delivered here:

The GPS panel is now Compose, as described last time.
The map follows the screen’s lifecycle through a shared observer.
Address lookups use the non-blocking geocoder on Android 13+ and run only after you move 25 m.
Saving a location reuses the shared database.
New tests: GeoDistanceTest and SpeedometerDialTest.
The README is updated.

Presented file
Phase 8b is in positional-phase8b.tar.gz: extract it at the repo root; it contains only changed and new files. I couldn’t compile it here (no Android SDK), so CI is the real check; the 8a build passed CI.

Panels

Shared map layout: a new MapPanel.kt now holds the map layout, toolbar, tool buttons and sheet handle used by all three map panels. The GPS screen was rebuilt on it without changing what it does.
Trail panel: now in Compose. The list of trail points opens as a bottom sheet in portrait and sits beside the map in landscape. Long-pressing a point gives navigate, share, copy and delete. Choosing a marker icon is now a small grid dialog instead of the old popup window.
Measure panel: now in Compose. The name, point count and distances show in a card at the bottom. That card sits above the bottom bar, so the old code that tracked the bar’s size is gone.
Data and bug fixes

Trail points update live: they now come from Room as a Flow. Previously every load, save and delete opened and closed its own database. Now one database stays open for the current trail, and it is closed before that trail is deleted.
Crash on Android 7–10 fixed: TrailPoint’s name and note getters used a Java method that only exists from Android 11. Phone or emulator testing on those versions would have crashed on the trail panel.
Distances: one shared DistanceText formatter now handles trail, measure and direction distances. Direction used to switch from feet to miles at 1000 m; all three now switch at one mile.
Navigation links: navigate and share go through a shared MapIntents helper. If Google Maps isn’t installed, it falls back to a generic geo: link.
Bottom bar callback: the panels now tell MainActivity to show or hide the bar through a new BottomBarHost interface, replacing BottomSheetSlide.
Cleanup

The timeline list library is removed from build.gradle.
Strings and dimensions that nothing uses any more are removed from every language.
New tests: DistanceTextTest, and a path-length test added to GeoDistanceTest.
The README is updated.
